Definition: from a derivative of G1476; a support, i.e. (figuratively) basis:--ground.
BiblicalUsage: Hedraioma is a support, a stay, the ground a thing stands on, and it appears once, for the church itself. In 1 Timothy 3:15 Paul writes so that Timothy may know how to behave in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the church is not the truth itself, it is the pillar that holds the truth up where people can see it, and a pillar that leans is no use to anyone.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
